clue.text: Be in time for a round

blocks.note: first meaning: to get to a train or bus before it leaves
second meaning: a song for several voices entering in turn, often with a comic twist

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests arriving punctually for a round of drinks or golf; a round here is a kind of part-song.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to reach a departing train or bus in time, and the noun is an old kind of humorous part-song sung in rounds.

clue.text: Not on, in church, to drink up its contents

definitions.text: Not on, in church, to drink up its contents

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means its letters sit inside the other's
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
a switch that is not on is off
to tope is an old verb for drinking heavily

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is told not to drink something up in church.
explanation.walkthrough: To tope is an old word for drinking heavily. Read whole, the clue also describes the pot, a vessel whose contents are there to be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot that holds the brewed beverage is a vessel whose contents are poured out and drunk.

clue.text: Sort of square aperture in the gunwale?

definitions.text: Sort of square aperture in the gunwale?

blocks.note: a T-square is a kind of square used in technical drawing
an aperture is an opening

explanation.surface: A boatbuilder describes a squared-off opening cut through the top edge of a boat's side.
explanation.walkthrough: T plus HOLE gives THOLE. The question mark admits the stretch: a thole is the pin set in the gunwale, the top edge of a boat's side, as a pivot for an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: A thole is a peg fixed in a rowing boat's upper edge to hold an oar in place while rowing.

clue.text: Prophet detailed to whistle for a water-carrier

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

blocks.note: Hosea is an Old Testament prophet, with its last letter removed
a pipe is a simple whistle

explanation.surface: A prophet is assigned to whistle up someone to fetch water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'assigned', but it means de-tailed: HOSEA loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible tube used in the garden conveys water from a tap to plants or a car.

clue.text: A signal to members longing for home

indicators.note: broken into members, or limbs, the letters are separated and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A homesick person sends a signal to the members of their family.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant homesickness, a yearning to return to one's native place, before widening to wistfulness for the past.

clue.text: An element of the new age

blocks.note: N is a common abbreviation for new
an eon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: Something is called a key part of the New Age movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The new age' reads like the hippy movement; split it as new, N, and age, EON.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chemical element, the inert noble gas that glows red in advertising signs.

clue.text: Graphic representation of hotel suite

indicators.note: a re-presentation sets the same letters out again in a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hotel brochure shows a vivid picture of one of its suites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graphic representation' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Graphic', used as a noun for a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark outline image of a figure, usually in profile, is a kind of picture or visual image.

clue.text: Its security is guaranteed by a fluke

definitions.text: Its security is guaranteed by a fluke

blocks.clueFragment: Its security is guaranteed by a fluke
blocks.note: surface reading: something stays safe only through sheer luck
setter's reading: a fluke is the flat blade on each arm of a ship's mooring device, which digs into the seabed

explanation.walkthrough: A fluke usually means a lucky chance; here it is the barbed blade that bites into the sea floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy hooked device holds a ship fast because its blades grip the seabed.

clue.text: 'Bull's-eye' Birkenhead, master craftsman

blocks.note: the gold is the centre of an archery target
F. E. Smith, the lawyer and politician, became Lord Birkenhead

explanation.surface: A master craftsman from the town of Birkenhead is nicknamed Bull's-eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town near Liverpool, but here it is the title of F. E. Smith, Lord Chancellor in the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker in precious metal is a skilled artisan, and the guild word master fits such a trade.

clue.text: Cancel article removed from almanac

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of its letters

blocks.note: an annual is a yearly publication, like an almanac
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor cancels an article that was dropped from the almanac.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNUAL loses one A to leave ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare a marriage or contract void is to cancel it officially.

clue.text: Infantry weapon for giving support

blocks.note: the foot are foot soldiers, and the infantry's weapon is the foot's
a tool is slang for a weapon, especially a gun

explanation.surface: A weapon issued to infantry for use in support.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Infantry weapon' as the foot's tool. The definition is a phrase describing the answer's purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A low stool to rest the feet on is a piece of furniture whose job is to hold up the legs.

clue.text: Stop American carnivore outside pound

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps round it

blocks.note: a coon is short for raccoon, an American mammal
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep an American predator from straying outside its pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop is a punctuation mark here, not an order to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: In punctuation, a stop is any mark that pauses or ends a sentence, and this two-dot mark is one.

clue.text: Grant immunity to former redcap appearing in film

indicators.note: something appearing in a film sits inside it

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
redcaps are British military police, from their red caps
ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A retired military policeman is let off after turning up in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cover on their caps.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation or liability, which is to excuse them by special dispensation.

clue.text: Gigantic as Caesar bestriding the narrow world?

definitions.text: as Caesar bestriding the narrow world?

blocks.note: first meaning: enormous

blocks.clueFragment: as Caesar bestriding the narrow world?
blocks.note: second meaning, by allusion: Cassius in Shakespeare says Caesar bestrides the narrow world like the giant statue of Rhodes

explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is Julius Caesar, Act 1: 'he doth bestride the narrow world like a Colossus', the huge statue at Rhodes.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the giant bronze statue of Rhodes and means vast or huge in size.

clue.text: Decree to restrain nobleman, an administrator of finance

indicators.note: to restrain something is to hold it within, so these letters enclose the next

blocks.note: an act is a law or decree
a count is a European nobleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decree is passed to curb a nobleman, a man who controls the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' looks like part of the definition but is a piece of the wordplay; the definition starts after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who keeps and audits financial records manages money matters for clients or a firm.

clue.text: Patrol guarding spot for a dip

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it guards, so these letters go round the next

blocks.note: a picket is a small patrol or guard
a pock is a spot or pustule

explanation.surface: A patrol keeps watch over a good place to go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: A dip is slang for a thief who steals from pockets, not a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: In thieves' slang a dip is someone who steals from people's pockets in crowds.

clue.text: Ready to pay this for poor chap's pudding?

blocks.note: plain reading: ready is cash, so this is the amount charged when paying in ready money
setter's whimsy: a hard-up man's dessert would be cheap rice pudding

explanation.walkthrough: Ready means ready money, cash. The second half splits the answer into a poor man's pudding of rice.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure charged to a buyer settling immediately in money rather than on credit or hire purchase.

clue.text: Fish, possibly, for evidence

blocks.note: first meaning: Pisces, the Fishes, is a zodiac symbol
second meaning: an indication or trace

explanation.surface: Someone goes fishing for evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a verb; it is Pisces, one of the twelve of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces is one of the zodiac's twelve divisions, and the same word means a mark or indication that something exists.

clue.text: Fruit producer's blunder in Parliamentary victory

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: Naseby, 1645, was the decisive Parliamentarian victory of the English Civil War
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A fruit grower makes a gaffe during a Parliamentary triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit producer's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical American evergreen also called sapodilla bears sweet brown edible fruits, so it is a fruiting tree.

clue.text: Bottomless depravity leads to a storm in the benefice

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, so it is cut off

blocks.note: vice is depravity, here without its final letter
taken as written
to rage or a rage is a storm of anger

explanation.surface: Endless wickedness causes uproar in a parish.
explanation.walkthrough: VICE loses its last letter to give VIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefice is a church living held by a parish priest, and this word names such a living as well as the priest's house.

clue.text: Projection may be a bit of a bore, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so a word stands for its sound-alike

blocks.note: first meaning: something that sticks out
second meaning, by sound: bore is heard as boar, and the long sticking-out tooth is part of a wild pig

explanation.surface: Someone's protruding feature is a little tedious, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Bore sounds like boar; the long tooth that sticks out of a boar's mouth is a bit of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed tooth that sticks out from the mouth of a boar, elephant or walrus is a protrusion.

clue.text: Luminaries of the acting profession?

blocks.note: surface reading: the star performers of the stage
setter's reading: literal lights, the lamps set along the front edge of a stage

explanation.walkthrough: Luminaries usually means celebrities; here it means sources of light, specifically those at the front of a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The row of lamps along the front of a theatre stage illuminates performers, and stands for the stage as a career.

clue.text: Make a hole in someone's capital

definitions.text: Make a hole in someone's capital

blocks.clueFragment: Make a hole in someone's capital
blocks.note: surface reading: to dent a person's savings
setter's reading: capital is the head, and the surgeon bores through the skull

explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money; it is the head, from Latin caput.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cut a disc of bone out of the skull with a surgical saw.

clue.text: Abbreviated clothes not extremely obvious

indicators.note: abbreviated means cut short, so the end is lost
the extremes of a word are its two end letters

blocks.note: apparel is clothing, here shortened by its last letter
the first and last letters of not

explanation.surface: Skimpy clothing that is not especially conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: APPAREL loses its L, then the outer letters of 'not' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clearly visible or plainly understood is evident, plain or manifest.

clue.text: Star secures first-class mark

blocks.note: first meaning: the brightest star in a constellation
second meaning: the top grade awarded for work

explanation.surface: A star pupil achieves top marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek first letter labels the brightest star of a constellation and is also the highest grade in marking.

clue.text: Boy sailor carries a big trunk in Africa

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within

blocks.note: Bob is a boy's name
taken as written
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A young sailor hauls a large chest across Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The trunk is a tree trunk, not luggage, and the A sits just after the boy's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This African tree is famous for its enormously thick, swollen stem that stores water.

clue.text: Put up writer, say, up for a spree

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up turns it bottom to top, so backwards
read upwards in a down entry, so backwards

blocks.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
e.g., for example, means say

explanation.surface: An author is accommodated, then goes off on a bender.
explanation.walkthrough: NIB reversed gives BIN and EG reversed gives GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of excessive eating or drinking is an indulgent spree or bender.

clue.text: Greyish, because extremely hazy

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: as means because
the outer letters of hazy

explanation.surface: Something looks greyish because it is very misty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'because' does double duty here: it supplies AS rather than merely linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash from a fire is pale grey, so something coloured like ash is grey-toned.

clue.text: Pandarus takes the King inside to titivate

indicators.note: to take someone in is to hold them within, so these letters wrap round the next
inside confirms that the royal letter sits within the go-between's letters

blocks.note: Pandarus, go-between in Troilus and Cressida, gave us the word pander
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: Pandarus brings the king indoors to smarten him up.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside PIMP. To titivate is to spruce oneself up.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to make small finishing touches to one's appearance, to preen or smarten up.

clue.text: A blemish in the sailor king, never to be found at the port

definitions.text: never to be found at the port

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: surface padding: the article only makes the sentence read naturally
AB is a sailor and ER is a king, Edward Rex
a stain is a blemish

explanation.surface: A sailor king with a flaw never goes ashore at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The port is the fortified wine passed round after dinner, not the harbour where a sailor would go ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refuses all alcohol, so would never be seen at the port decanter after dinner.

clue.text: Cook nearby with the hard biscuit

indicators.note: to cook something, as in cooking the books, is to tamper with it and rework it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: bake the hard biscuit nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' seems to be the baking instruction; it is the anagram signal. Here 'with' links the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crisp Scottish caraway-flavoured biscuit, named after the surgeon John Abernethy.

clue.text: Polish producer engineers return to Yugoslavian capital

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so backwards
a capital is a word's head, its opening letter

blocks.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
the opening letter of Yugoslavian

explanation.surface: A Polish manufacturer's engineers go back to Belgrade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is polish, to shine. Yugoslavian capital is not Belgrade but its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The abrasive powder of corundum is used on boards and cloth for smoothing and shining surfaces.
